verses.1: Then Joshua will call upon Reuveni, Gadhi, and Hachi Mata Menashe.
verses.2: And he said to them, “You have obeyed all that Moses commanded you as servants of the LORD. And you have heard my voice in everything I have commanded you.”
verses.3: You have not abandoned your brothers over these many days until today. You have kept the commandments of the LORD your God.
verses.4: And now, let Jehovah your God be with your brothers, just as He has spoken to them. Now go back to your homes, to the land that belongs to you. This land was given to you by Moses, the servant of Jehovah, across the Jordan River.
verses.5: Only those who strictly keep these commandments and laws will be able to fulfill Moses’ commandment: “Love the LORD your God, and follow all His commands. Keep His laws, and serve Him with all your heart and soul.”
verses.6: And Joshua blessed them, and sent them away. Then they went to their camps.
verses.7: And Moses gave half of the grain to the men, while Joshua gave half of it to their brothers across the Jordan River. And even though Joshua sent them away to their camps, he still blessed them.
verses.8: And he said to them, “With great wealth, return to your homes. You will receive a large amount of money, gold, silver, and other treasures. Divide among yourselves the spoils of your enemies.”
verses.9: And they returned, and went away. The sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad, along with half of the tribe of Manasseh, left from among the Israelites who were in the land of Canaan, to go to the land of Gilgal, to their own inheritance. This inheritance was not yet taken possession of by them, according to Jehovah’s command, in the hands of Moses.
verses.10: And they went to Gilgal in the land of Canaan. There, the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad built an altar on the banks of the Jordan River. It was a great altar for sacrifices.
verses.11: And the children of Israel heard these words: “Look, Reuben and Gad have taken half of the livestock and have carried it to Canaan, along with the rest of the livestock. They brought it across the Jordan River to the land of Israel.”
verses.12: And the children of Israel heard this. All the tribes of Israel gathered together to go up onto the mountain.
verses.13: And the children of Israel sent men to Ruben and Gad, as well as to half of Manasseh’s tribe. They went to the land of Gilgal, where they took Pinhaeus, son of Elazar, the priest.
verses.14: And twelve men went with him. Each of them led a group of people from the house of their ancestors. These were the leaders of all the tribes of Israel.
verses.15: And they went to the children of Reuben and to the children of Gad, and to half the tribe of Manasseh. They went to the land of Gilgalad. And they spoke to them these words:
verses.16: So said all the people of Jehovah: What is this high place that you have built for yourselves as a worship site before the God of Israel? Today, from behind Jehovah’s back, you will be brought back here. This high place will become a sacrifice for you, for your rebellion against Jehovah today.
verses.17: We have been defiled by the sin of those who did not cleanse ourselves from it until today. And there was punishment upon them in the sight of Jehovah.
verses.18: And you shall return today from the side of Jehovah. Today, you will rebel against Jehovah. And after that, all the tribes of Israel will be punished.
verses.19: But if the land that belongs to you is unclean, then go to the land that belongs to Jehovah. That land is located there, where Jehovah’s temple stands. Stay in that land. Do not rebel against us. And let your children also not rebel against us. We will give them a sacrifice that is separate from the sacrifices offered to Jehovah, our God.
verses.20: Hallow, son of Zerah, who was above all others in his own generation and among all the people of Israel. He was a great man, and he was not like any other person.
verses.21: And the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad, along with half of the men of Manasseh, spoke to the leaders of all the Israelites.
verses.22: God, Jehovah, God, Jehovah! He knows everything. Israel will know whether it is in rebellion or in peace. May He not save us today.
verses.23: Let us offer sacrifices to God for our return from the presence of Jehovah. And if we want to offer sacrifices of thanksgiving and offerings, then let us do so. But if we want to offer sacrifices of peace offerings, then Jehovah will accept them.
verses.24: And if there’s no need to worry about what people say, then we shall do this: “Afterward, your children will say to us, ‘What are you going to do?’ And let the LORD, the God of Israel, decide.”
verses.25: And Jehovah has divided between us and you, children of Reuben and children of Gad, the land of Jordan. You have no share in Jehovah’s inheritance. May your children be destroyed among you, so that I will not have to fear Jehovah.
verses.26: And it was said, “Let us be allowed to build our own altar. It should not be used for worshiping God.”
verses.27: For he is witness among us, among you, and among our gods. He will judge us in his own way, through our offerings and sacrifices. And they will not say, “You have no share in the Lord.”
verses.28: And it was said, “Let them say to us and to our ancestors from now on: ‘See how the idols of Yahweh were made by our ancestors. They were not made for worshiping God.’ For they are still among us and among you.”
verses.29: May we be freed from this state of rebellion against Jehovah. May we return today from our rebellion against Jehovah, so that we can build an altar for worship, as a sacrifice to Jehovah our God, who is located before His temple.
verses.30: And Pinchas, the priest, and the leaders of the congregation, and the heads of thousands of Israel, who heard what the sons of Reuben, the sons of Gad, and the sons of Manasseh said, were pleased with it.
verses.31: And Pinchas, son of Elazar, the priest, said to the sons of Reuben, and to the sons of Gad, and to the sons of Manasseh: “Today we know that among us is Jehovah, who has not been exalted above this high place. Therefore, Jehovah saved the children of Israel from their enemies.”
verses.32: And Pinchas, son of Elazar the priest and chief among the sons of Reuben and Gad from the land of Gilgalad, went to the land of Canaan, to the children of Israel. And they obeyed his commands.
verses.33: And this pleased the children of Israel. God blessed the children of Israel, and they did not say anything to the priests about attacking the land that was inhabited by the descendants of Reuben and Gad.
verses.34: And the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad called out to the priest, “See, He is among us! For Jehovah is the God.”
